The Glass Heron
Chapter 13: Cloves and Lamp Oil
Previous Chapter | Table of Contents | Next Chapter

Translator: Quill

The fortune teller turned the pin over in her fingers, and the silver thread on the tablecloth seemed to shiver in sympathy.

“Where did you get this?” she asked.

“It was my mother’s,” Ilsa said. “She left it in a drawer with a note that said only: when the lanterns burn blue, take it to the woman with the clove tent.”

The old woman laughed, a dry sound like pages turning. “And have the lanterns burned blue?”

“Last night. Every one of them, for the length of a breath.”

Tobin shifted on his cushion. “I saw it too. I thought it was a trick of the river mist.”

“It was no trick.” The fortune teller set the pin down between them and folded her hands. “Listen carefully, both of you, because I will only say this once, and the walls of this tent are thinner than they look.”

Outside, the knife grinder’s wheel stopped turning.
